headline: Sound Like a Native · Master
threshold: Carry clear consonant–vowel patterns into natural Spanish words, phrases, and conversation.

lessons.title: Natural statement contours
lessons.objective: Practise a short statement using a consistent regional model.
lessons.focus: Start with ma mi mu me mo, then use a consistent statement contour from your chosen speaker model. Keep final vowels clear without making every sentence end identically.

words.es: Hoy tengo tiempo para revisar el plan.
words.en: Today I have time to review the plan.

words.es: Mañana debo salir antes de la reunión.
words.en: Tomorrow I must leave before the meeting.

words.es: Explico la diferencia con una voz tranquila.
words.en: I explain the difference in a calm voice.

words.es: Mi compañera escucha el mensaje completo antes de responder.
words.en: My colleague listens to the whole message before answering.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, practise a short statement using a consistent regional model. Use the scene: A calm explanation. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Practise a short statement using a consistent regional model.

examples.es: Hoy tengo tiempo para revisar el plan.
examples.en: Today I have time to review the plan.

examples.es: Mañana debo salir antes de la reunión.
examples.en: Tomorrow I must leave before the meeting.

lessons.title: Questions in context
lessons.objective: Compare question contours across intent and regional models.
lessons.focus: After ta ti tu te to, compare a yes/no question and an information question. Match a named speaker model and intention; do not assume every Spanish question has one rising contour.

words.es: Quiero confirmar la visita de mañana.
words.en: I want to confirm tomorrow's visit.

words.es: Primero hago una pregunta que admite sí o no.
words.en: First I ask a question that allows yes or no.

words.es: Pregunto si mi amiga viene mañana.
words.en: I ask whether my friend is coming tomorrow.

words.es: Su respuesta es que todavía no conoce la hora.
words.en: Her answer is that she does not know the time yet.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, compare question contours across intent and regional models. Use the scene: Two questions about tomorrow. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Compare question contours across intent and regional models.

examples.es: Quiero confirmar la visita de mañana.
examples.en: I want to confirm tomorrow's visit.

examples.es: Primero hago una pregunta que admite sí o no.
examples.en: First I ask a question that allows yes or no.

lessons.title: Focus and emphasis
lessons.objective: Move emphasis to express a correction or contrast.
lessons.focus: Keep the consonant-linked warm-up, then move focus within Yo pedí té. Contrast the intended correction without shouting or exaggerating every word.

words.es: El camarero deja un café junto a mi plato.
words.en: The waiter leaves a coffee beside my plate.

words.es: Le digo que pedí té, no café.
words.en: I tell him that I ordered tea, not coffee.

words.es: Otra persona pregunta quién hizo el pedido.
words.en: Another person asks who placed the order.

words.es: Aclaro que yo pedí el té.
words.en: I clarify that I ordered the tea.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, move emphasis to express a correction or contrast. Use the scene: Tea instead of coffee. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Move emphasis to express a correction or contrast.

examples.en: The waiter leaves a coffee beside my plate.

examples.es: Le digo que pedí té, no café.
examples.en: I tell him that I ordered tea, not coffee.

lessons.title: Lists and unfinished thoughts
lessons.objective: Use voice and pauses to signal continuation.
lessons.focus: Practise la li lu le lo, then organize a list with continuation and completion cues from a speaker model. Use pauses to preserve grouping, not to break every word apart.

words.es: Preparo una lista antes de ir al mercado.
words.en: I prepare a list before going to the market.

words.es: Necesito pan, queso y fruta para la reunión.
words.en: I need bread, cheese, and fruit for the meeting.

words.es: Hago una pausa porque todavía falta algo.
words.en: I pause because something is still missing.

words.es: Mi hermano pregunta si ya terminé la lista.
words.en: My brother asks whether I have finished the list.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, use voice and pauses to signal continuation. Use the scene: A shopping list that is not finished. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Use voice and pauses to signal continuation.

examples.en: I prepare a list before going to the market.

lessons.title: Polite requests
lessons.objective: Match rhythm and intonation to a courteous request.
lessons.focus: Use pa pi pu pe po to settle the vowel sequence, then model a polite request in a whole phrase. Compare a direct command and a courteous request without claiming intonation alone makes a phrase polite.

words.es: El restaurante tiene mucho ruido esta noche.
words.en: The restaurant is very noisy tonight.

words.es: Pido ayuda a la persona que organiza las mesas.
words.en: I ask the person who organizes the tables for help.

words.es: Le pregunto si podemos sentarnos cerca de la ventana.
words.en: I ask whether we can sit near the window.

words.es: Añado por favor y explico que buscamos un lugar tranquilo.
words.en: I add please and explain that we are looking for a quiet place.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, match rhythm and intonation to a courteous request. Use the scene: Asking for a quiet table. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Match rhythm and intonation to a courteous request.

examples.en: The restaurant is very noisy tonight.

examples.es: Pido ayuda a la persona que organiza las mesas.
examples.en: I ask the person who organizes the tables for help.

lessons.title: Emotion without losing clarity
lessons.objective: Compare surprise, reassurance, and neutral delivery.
lessons.focus: Warm up with sa si su se so. Use the same meaningful phrase with neutral, surprised, and reassuring delivery; preserve the words and avoid a single caricatured contour.

words.es: Recibo un mensaje que cambia la hora del viaje.
words.en: I receive a message that changes the trip time.

words.es: Mi primera reacción es de sorpresa.
Pregunto si de verdad salimos más temprano.
words.en: I ask whether we really are leaving earlier.

words.es: Mi amigo me dice que todavía podemos llegar.
words.en: My friend tells me that we can still make it.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, compare surprise, reassurance, and neutral delivery. Use the scene: Surprise and reassurance. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Compare surprise, reassurance, and neutral delivery.

examples.en: I receive a message that changes the trip time.

examples.es: Mi primera reacción es de sorpresa.
examples.en: My first reaction is surprise.

lessons.title: Short shadowing
lessons.objective: Echo a short phrase with one sound and one rhythm target.
lessons.focus: Use ka ki ku ke ko as a controlled warm-up, then echo one short meaningful phrase after the model pauses. Choose one articulation target and one rhythm target at a time.

words.es: Escucho una frase corta antes de intentar repetirla.
words.en: I listen to a short phrase before trying to repeat it.

words.es: El modelo dice que quiere una copa de agua.
words.en: The model says that they would like a glass of water.

words.es: Espero una pausa y repito el mensaje completo.
words.en: I wait for a pause and repeat the complete message.

words.es: Primero presto atención a una palabra difícil.
words.en: First I pay attention to a difficult word.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, echo a short phrase with one sound and one rhythm target. Use the scene: Echoing one useful phrase. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Echo a short phrase with one sound and one rhythm target.

examples.es: Escucho una frase corta antes de intentar repetirla.
examples.en: I listen to a short phrase before trying to repeat it.

examples.es: El modelo dice que quiere una copa de agua.
examples.en: The model says that they would like a glass of water.

lessons.title: Longer shadowing
lessons.objective: Keep phrase groups across a short paragraph.
lessons.focus: Warm up with ga gui gu gue go. Listen once for meaning, then echo short phrase groups; increase chunk length only while clear speech and meaning remain.

words.es: Escucho un mensaje completo antes de dividirlo.
words.en: I listen to a complete message before dividing it.

words.es: La lectura explica cómo llegar a una reunión del grupo.
words.en: The reading explains how to get to a group meeting.

words.es: Marco una pausa después del lugar de encuentro.
words.en: I mark a pause after the meeting place.

words.es: Luego repito la parte que indica la hora de salida.
words.en: Then I repeat the part that gives the departure time.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, keep phrase groups across a short paragraph. Use the scene: A longer message in short groups. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Keep phrase groups across a short paragraph.

examples.en: I listen to a complete message before dividing it.

examples.es: La lectura explica cómo llegar a una reunión del grupo.
examples.en: The reading explains how to get to a group meeting.

lessons.title: Read-aloud transfer
lessons.objective: Use sound habits in a passage not drilled beforehand.
lessons.focus: Use cha chi chu che cho, then read this new passage once for meaning and once for delivery. Pick one sound target and preserve natural stress across the whole reading.

words.es: La encargada abre la tienda antes de que llegue el grupo.
words.en: The person in charge opens the shop before the group arrives.

words.es: Un niño entra con una mochila pequeña.
words.en: A child comes in with a small backpack.

words.es: Busca una llave que perdió durante el camino.
words.en: He looks for a key he lost on the way.

words.es: La encargada escucha la descripción y revisa el mostrador.
words.en: The person in charge listens to the description and checks the counter.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, use sound habits in a passage not drilled beforehand. Use the scene: A new passage about a shop. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Use sound habits in a passage not drilled beforehand.

examples.en: The person in charge opens the shop before the group arrives.

lessons.title: Spontaneous retelling
lessons.objective: Retell a message while preserving meaning and clear stress.
lessons.focus: Start with ma mi mu me mo, then read, hide, and retell. Preserve who, what, and when while carrying the vowel pattern into unrehearsed speech.

words.es: La vecina deja un mensaje sobre un paquete.
words.en: The neighbor leaves a message about a package.

words.es: Dice que no estará en casa durante la tarde.
words.en: She says that she will not be home during the afternoon.

words.es: Me pide que reciba el paquete si llaman a la puerta.
words.en: She asks me to receive the package if someone knocks at the door.

words.es: También explica dónde puede dejarlo el repartidor.
words.en: She also explains where the delivery person can leave it.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, retell a message while preserving meaning and clear stress. Use the scene: Retelling a neighbor's message. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Retell a message while preserving meaning and clear stress.

examples.es: La vecina deja un mensaje sobre un paquete.
examples.en: The neighbor leaves a message about a package.

examples.es: Dice que no estará en casa durante la tarde.
examples.en: She says that she will not be home during the afternoon.

lessons.title: Names and addresses
lessons.objective: Stay clear when the listener needs precise information.
lessons.focus: Use na ni nu ne no, then slow only the information that needs precision. Keep final consonants and word boundaries intelligible in names and numbers.

words.es: Doy mi nombre cuando llamo para confirmar la entrega.
words.en: I give my name when I call to confirm the delivery.

words.es: La persona me pide la dirección completa.
words.en: The person asks me for the complete address.

words.es: Digo la calle, el número y la puerta.
words.en: I say the street, the number, and the door.

words.es: Después separo el nombre de la calle del número del edificio.
words.en: Then I separate the street name from the building number.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, stay clear when the listener needs precise information. Use the scene: Confirming an address. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Stay clear when the listener needs precise information.

examples.es: Doy mi nombre cuando llamo para confirmar la entrega.
examples.en: I give my name when I call to confirm the delivery.

examples.es: La persona me pide la dirección completa.
examples.en: The person asks me for the complete address.

lessons.title: Numbers and times
lessons.objective: Keep number contrasts clear inside normal phrases.
lessons.focus: Practise trece/treinta and quince/cincuenta as word contrasts inside messages. A fast drill result is secondary to the listener identifying the correct number.

words.es: La reunión empieza a las trece horas.
words.en: The meeting starts at thirteen hundred hours.

words.es: Una compañera entiende treinta y pide una aclaración.
words.en: A colleague hears thirty and asks for clarification.

words.es: Repito trece dentro de una frase completa.
words.en: I repeat thirteen inside a complete sentence.

words.es: Después confirmamos que asistirán quince personas.
words.en: Then we confirm that fifteen people will attend.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, keep number contrasts clear inside normal phrases. Use the scene: Thirteen or thirty. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Keep number contrasts clear inside normal phrases.

examples.en: The meeting starts at thirteen hundred hours.

examples.es: Una compañera entiende treinta y pide una aclaración.
examples.en: A colleague hears thirty and asks for clarification.

lessons.title: Travel conversation
lessons.objective: Use the sound targets in a practical exchange.
lessons.focus: Use a tap/trill comparison warm-up, then handle an unrehearsed change to the reservation. Keep the time and price clear even when your response becomes longer.

words.es: Llamo para confirmar una reserva antes del viaje.
words.en: I call to confirm a reservation before the trip.

words.es: La empleada explica que hay un cambio de hora.
words.en: The employee explains that there is a change of time.

words.es: Le pregunto si el precio sigue siendo el mismo.
words.en: I ask whether the price is still the same.

words.es: Su respuesta es que la reserva mantiene todas las condiciones.
words.en: Her answer is that the reservation keeps all the same conditions.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, use the sound targets in a practical exchange. Use the scene: A reservation with a changed time. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Use the sound targets in a practical exchange.

examples.en: I call to confirm a reservation before the trip.

examples.es: La empleada explica que hay un cambio de hora.
examples.en: The employee explains that there is a change of time.

lessons.title: Work conversation
lessons.objective: Speak clearly while explaining a routine problem.
lessons.focus: Use pa pi pu pe po, then explain the work problem in clear meaning groups. Do not trade clarity for speed when adding a reason or next step.

words.es: El equipo no responde cuando comienza la prueba.
words.en: The equipment does not respond when the test begins.

words.es: Le explico el problema a mi compañera sin culpar a nadie.
words.en: I explain the problem to my colleague without blaming anyone.

words.es: Primero digo qué paso funciona y cuál falla.
words.en: First I say which step works and which one fails.

words.es: Después comparo el mensaje de hoy con el de ayer.
words.en: Then I compare today's message with yesterday's.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, speak clearly while explaining a routine problem. Use the scene: Explaining a routine work problem. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Speak clearly while explaining a routine problem.

examples.en: The equipment does not respond when the test begins.

lessons.title: Repair and clarification
lessons.objective: Clarify a message naturally when misunderstood.
lessons.focus: Warm up with da di du de do. Repair only the part that caused difficulty, changing pace or wording while preserving the intended meaning.

words.es: Mi amiga entiende una palabra distinta en mi mensaje.
words.en: My friend understands a different word in my message.

words.es: Su pregunta me ayuda a identificar el detalle confuso.
words.en: Her question helps me identify the confusing detail.

words.es: Le digo qué quise decir y repito esa parte.
words.en: I tell her what I meant and repeat that part.

words.es: Después explico el mismo sentido con otras palabras.
words.en: Then I explain the same meaning in other words.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, clarify a message naturally when misunderstood. Use the scene: Repairing a misunderstood message. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Clarify a message naturally when misunderstood.

examples.en: My friend understands a different word in my message.

examples.es: Su pregunta me ayuda a identificar el detalle confuso.
examples.en: Her question helps me identify the confusing detail.

lessons.title: Regional y/ll listening
lessons.objective: Recognize examples from named regions without mixing every feature.
lessons.focus: Keep a consistent production model for y/ll and compare named regional examples only when real reviewed audio is available. Without those clips, use this as a transcript and discussion task, not a listening test.

words.es: Dos personas describen la misma calle en una conversación.
words.en: Two people describe the same street in a conversation.

words.es: Cada voz refleja una historia y una región diferentes.
words.en: Each voice reflects a different history and region.

words.es: Las dos mencionan una llave que encontraron cerca de la puerta.
words.en: Both mention a key they found near the door.

words.es: Una amiga me explica de qué región es su familia.
words.en: A friend explains which region her family comes from.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, recognize examples from named regions without mixing every feature. Use the scene: Different voices, the same street. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Recognize examples from named regions without mixing every feature.

lessons.title: Regional s and j listening
lessons.objective: Recognize selected variations in real, reviewed recordings.
lessons.focus: Compare regional s and j only with identified speaker examples. Keep the consonant-linked production pattern; do not teach dropping consonants as a universal shortcut to sounding natural.

words.es: Mis amigos dejan un mensaje sobre una reunión en el jardín.
words.en: My friends leave a message about a gathering in the garden.

words.es: Quiero reconocer la información aunque cambie la voz que la dice.
words.en: I want to recognize the information even if the voice saying it changes.

words.es: El contexto me ayuda a entender dónde debemos encontrarnos.
words.en: The context helps me understand where we should meet.

words.es: Algunas realizaciones de ciertos sonidos dependen de la región.
words.en: Some realizations of certain sounds depend on the region.

lessons.title: Personal sound priorities
lessons.objective: Choose two recurring pronunciation habits from real evidence.
lessons.focus: Select two priorities from real self-listening or instructor observations. Use the relevant consonant-linked row, then test the movement in a new phrase instead of drilling everything faster.

words.es: Escucho un intento anterior antes de elegir la práctica de hoy.
words.en: I listen to an earlier attempt before choosing today's practice.

words.es: Busco un hábito de sonido que puedo describir con claridad.
words.en: I look for a sound habit that I can describe clearly.

words.es: También elijo una frase cuyo ritmo quiero mejorar.
words.en: I also choose a phrase whose rhythm I want to improve.

words.es: Repito una palabra dentro de un patrón que ya conozco.
words.en: I repeat a word within a pattern that I already know.

lessons.title: Conversation under a complication
lessons.objective: Maintain clear speech when a scene changes unexpectedly.
lessons.focus: Warm up with ka ki ku ke ko, then handle a complication without a script. Preserve the important consonants, numbers, and phrase boundaries while deciding what to do.

words.en: I am confirming an address during a call.

words.es: La persona interrumpe para explicar un cambio inesperado.
words.en: The person interrupts to explain an unexpected change.

words.es: El grupo ya no puede entrar por la puerta principal.
words.en: The group can no longer enter through the main door.

words.es: Pregunto qué otra opción permite llegar a tiempo.
words.en: I ask what other option allows us to arrive on time.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, maintain clear speech when a scene changes unexpectedly. Use the scene: An unexpected change during a call. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Maintain clear speech when a scene changes unexpectedly.

lessons.title: Final transfer portfolio
lessons.objective: Compare baseline and final speech using a clear review rubric.
lessons.focus: Choose your own consonant-linked warm-up, then compare baseline and final speech with specific observations. Use a new reading and an unexpected question; completion alone is not an assessed native accent.

words.es: Leo un texto nuevo antes de explicar el plan.
words.en: I read a new text before explaining the plan.

words.es: La lectura incluye un lugar, una hora y un cambio importante.
words.en: The reading includes a place, a time, and an important change.

words.es: Después aparto el texto y resumo la información.
words.en: Then I put the text aside and summarize the information.

words.es: Otra persona hace una pregunta que no he preparado.
words.en: Another person asks a question that I have not prepared.

grammar.focus: Meaningful communication: Compare baseline and final speech using a clear review rubric.
